BMEG 101.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
BMEG 101.description: Foundational material spanning the four streams of the BMEG undergraduate program. Topics include: sensors and instrumentation; biosignals; physiological modeling; biomechanics; biomaterials; cellular engineering; regenerative medicine; and engineering design in these contexts.

BMEG 102.title: Biomedical Engineering Lab
BMEG 102.description: Introduction to the breadth of laboratory and experimental techniques in biomedical engineering. Hydrogel design, genetic engineering of bacteria, bioinformatics pipeline construction, electrical instrumentation, and bioreactor design.

BMEG 200.title: Biomedical Engineering Bridge Module
BMEG 200.description: Core concepts of biomedical engineering with a focus on advanced biological concepts that are inherent in biomechanics analysis, biomaterials signals and systems, bioinformatics and cellular bioengineering.

BMEG 201.title: Technical Communication for Biomedical Engineers
BMEG 201.description: Report preparation, business correspondence, and oral presentation in biomedical engineering specific cases and projects. .
BMEG 201.prerequisiteText: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 112, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150

BMEG 210.title: Thermodynamics in Biomedical Engineering
BMEG 210.description: Work, heat and energy; material and energy balances; the first law and second law of thermodynamics; entropy and process reversibility; availability (energy) analysis; Hess's Law; thermodynamic properties of fluids; and applications to biomedical systems. .

BMEG 220.title: Circuits and Electromagnetics with Application to Biomedical Engineering
BMEG 220.description: Electromagnetic phenomena in the body; bioinstrumentation; electrostatic and electromagnetic fields, forces, capacitance and inductance; bio-effects of electromagnetic fields; and modelling electrical components of physiological and biomedical systems.
BMEG 220.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 158. All of MATH_V 253, MATH_V 256

BMEG 230.title: Biomechanics I
BMEG 230.description: Integrating the study of two dimensional movement of animals and humans with the study of the manner in which forces on biomechanical structures such as bones, ligaments, tendons, muscles and joints cause motion. Techniques of solid mechanics and two dimensional rigid body dynamics. Students who have received credit for MECH_V 435 cannot also receive credit for BMEG_V 230 or BMEG_V 330. .
BMEG 230.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BMEG_V 101, PHYS_V 170 or (b) all of APSC_V 101, BMEG_V 200, PHYS_V 170

BMEG 245.title: The Fundamental Units of Life: From Cells To Systems
BMEG 245.description: The structure and function of cells and how they are organized to generate tissues and organ systems

BMEG 250.title: Cellular Physiology and Biophysics
BMEG 250.description: Cellular structure and mechanisms of membrane transport, signal transduction, muscle mechanochemistry and neurotransmission. Structure and hierarchical organization up to the level of tissues. Light and electron microscopy. .

BMEG 257.title: Biomedical Engineering Design I
BMEG 257.description: Engineering design process for biomedical technologies. Practical skills in engineering design, computer aided design, electronic circuits, programming, and rapid prototyping in the context of biomedical technologies. Introduction to broader ethical and sustainability considerations for biomedical technology design.
BMEG 257.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BMEG_V 101, BMEG_V 102 or (b) all of APSC_V 101, BMEG_V 200, PHYS_V 159

BMEG 300.title: Topics in Biomedical Engineering I
BMEG 300.description: Lectures or projects on specialized topics in Biomedical Engineering at the 300-level.

BMEG 310.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics
BMEG 310.description: Principles behind the methods of bioinformatics. The use of bioinformatics databases and tools for solving problems in genomics, proteomics, structural biology and evolutionary biology. .
BMEG 310.prerequisiteText: BMEG_V 245 and one of CPEN_V 221, CPEN_V 223

BMEG 320.title: Bioengineering Feedback Systems and Controls
BMEG 320.description: Modelling, analysis and simulation of dynamic systems; system modelling by state space; linearization; feedback, stability and sensitivity; control system design. Examples from biological systems, assistive systems and biomedical equipment. .
BMEG 320.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BMEG_V 220 or (b) all of ELEC_V 221, ELEC_V 201, ELEC_V 202

BMEG 321.title: Biomedical Instrumentation
BMEG 321.description: Fundamental working principles of medical instruments used for measurements of nervous, respiratory and circulatory systems with focus on biopotential signals. Other topics include medical imaging, as well as minimally invasive and robotic surgery.
BMEG 321.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MATH_V 256 or (b) all of MATH_V 265, MATH_V 267; and either (a) BMEG_V 220 or (b) one of ELEC_V 211, PHYS_V 301 and one of ELEC_V 201, ELEC_V 204

BMEG 330.title: Biomechanics II
BMEG 330.description: Principles and common elements of sports-, orthopaedic-, injury- and cellular length-biomechanics. Improving sports performance and preventing overuse injuries through sports biomechanics, designing orthopaedic implants through orthopaedic biomechanics, preventing injuries through injury biomechanics and identifying and filtering cancerous blood cells through cellular biomechanics. Students who have received credit for MECH_V 435 cannot also receive credit for BMEG_V 230 or BMEG_V 330. .

BMEG 350.title: Human Structure/Function from Cells to Systems
BMEG 350.description: Human anatomy, histology and physiology with examples from biomedical engineering. Anatomical compartmentation and function regulation; homeostatic control systems, sensors and effectors; intercellular communication strategies; and cellular and organ function assessment. .

BMEG 357.title: Biomedical Engineering Design II
BMEG 357.description: Creating innovations in biomedical technologies. Supervised design process for clinical clients, involving the building, testing, and verification of prototypes with potential users. .

BMEG 371.title: Transport Phenomena within Cells and Tissues
BMEG 371.description: Fluid flow and mass transport analysis within healthy and diseased cells and tissues using mathematics. Drug delivery and tissue engineering. .
BMEG 371.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 253, MATH_V 217 and either (a) MATH_V 256 or (b) all of MATH_V 255, MATH_V 257

BMEG 372.title: Biomedical Materials and Drug Delivery
BMEG 372.description: Biomaterials science/engineering applied to design and synthesis of drug delivery systems. Biomaterial types, synthesis and testing; the use of biomaterials; biological response; biocompatibility and degradation; drug delivery systems; nanocarriers; modification of polymers; liposomes and micelles; nucleic acid, transdermal and oral delivery. .

BMEG 373.title: Microfluidics
BMEG 373.description: Advantages and disadvantages of miniaturization of complex fluid flow processes. Manipulating liquid flow; electrophoretic velocity and mobility; serial dilution; capillary electrophoresis; integrated microfluidic platforms; and blood and the motility of bacteria.

BMEG 374.title: Cellular Bioengineering: Laboratory & Design
BMEG 374.description: Fundamental genetic, molecular, and tissue engineering techniques. Design of experiments and tools related to these essential cellular bioengineering techniques. .

BMEG 400.title: Topics in Biomedical Engineering
BMEG 400.description: Lectures or projects on specialized topics in Biomedical Engineering.

BMEG 401.title: Economics of Healthcare Solutions
BMEG 401.description: Canadian and USA engineering economics in BME and healthcare systems. Economic equivalence, cost estimation, risk assessment, regulatory frameworks, economic optimization, intangible factors, ethics, sustainability, financial tools, commercialization and regulator regimes.

BMEG 402.title: Impact of Biomedical Engineering on Society, Sustainability and Environmental Stewardship
BMEG 402.description: Impact of biomedical engineering on health, safety, and political, cultural, economical and environmental implications of biomedical engineering design.

BMEG 410.title: Biomedical Equipment, Physiology, and Anatomy
BMEG 410.description: Principles and operation of biomedical equipment for cardiovascular system, respiratory system, renal dialysis, endoscopy, surgery, and imaging. Functional relationships of biomedical equipment to physiology and anatomy of major body systems.

BMEG 420.title: Medical Imaging
BMEG 420.description: Physical principles of ultrasound, magnetic resonance, computed tomography, X-ray projection imaging and molecular imaging in medical imaging for diagnostics, therapeutics and interventions.
BMEG 420.prerequisiteText: One of BMEG 220, BMEG 250 and one of BMEG 321, ELEC 371

BMEG 421.title: Linear Systems in Optics
BMEG 421.description: Linear system theory and Fourier Optics, applications in optics including wave propagation and image quality assessment.

BMEG 422.title: Modern Biomedical Optical Imaging
BMEG 422.description: Advanced multimodal optical imaging concepts, fundamental optics, optical OCT theories, advanced modern OCT technologies, and OCT application in clinical medicine and biomedical engineering.

BMEG 423.title: Clinical Informatics
BMEG 423.description: Fundamental concepts in clinical information systems, decision support, and mobile health. Application of information engineering to health care, including the management and use of patient health and well-being information.

BMEG 424.title: Genome Informatics
BMEG 424.description: Principles and best practices in analyzing genomics data. Genome architecture, mappability, repeat elements, ChIP-seq, open chromatin, histone modifications, single cell technologies, genome wide association studies, statistical analyses, computational analysis, data processing.

BMEG 425.title: Biomedical Robotics
BMEG 425.description: Biomedical robotics, mathematical fundamentals of kinematics, dynamics and control of robots by human operators, and applications of biomedical robotics.
BMEG 425.prerequisiteText: All of MATH_V 152, BMEG_V 321, and one of ELEC_V 221, BMEG_V 320

BMEG 426.title: Synthetic Biology Intensive
BMEG 426.description: Core skills in DNA device engineering, molecular biology, mammalian cell culture, and data analysis through a self-led, realworld experimental and scientific reporting journey.

BMEG 427.title: ImmunoEngineering
BMEG 427.description: Application of biomedical engineering principles to immunology. The immune system's role in biomedical challenges, and engineering applications with the immune system. Fundamental and applied lectures, case studies, and a project proposing biomedical solutions to immunology problems.

BMEG 428.title: Wearable Technology in Clinical Care
BMEG 428.description: Wearable health sensing technologies, computational techniques, and validation for real-world applications. Physiological responses, signal processing, machine learning, and clinical relevance, as well as a study project utilizing wearable sensors in clinical settings.

BMEG 429.title: Experimental Microfluidics for Bioanalytical Applications
BMEG 429.description: Practical training in microfluidic approaches for bioanalytical applications, covering fabrication, flow control, analysis, and experiment design. Includes hands-on lab sessions and studies applications in biomedicine, materials, and chemistry.

BMEG 455.title: Professionalism and Ethics in Biomedical Engineering
BMEG 455.description: Ethical, equity, and diversity issues and professionalism in Biomedical Engineering practice and design. Case studies and design projects will be used to expand on the foundation of biomedical engineering design, applying real-world ethical dilemmas including professional, medical, and research ethics. .

BMEG 456.title: Clinical and Industrial Biomedical Engineering
BMEG 456.description: Principles of clinical practice, Canadian healthcare system, medical approach to diagnosis, ethics and regulations for clinical trials, medical technology management, medical device development and standards, biostatistics. .

BMEG 457.title: Biomedical Engineering Design Project
BMEG 457.description: Capstone design and development of a practical biomedical device or system. Projects provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories.

BMEG 470.title: Cellular Responses to Forces and Biomaterials
BMEG 470.description: Mechanical forces and biomaterials regulating cellular functions critical to tissue development, regeneration and repair.

BMEG 474.title: Stem Cells and Regenerative Medicine
BMEG 474.description: Biology and applications of stem cells in regenerative medicine. Modelling human biology and disease in vitro and in vivo. Regulatory and commercialization pathways for regenerative medicine innovations. .

BMEG 490.title: Introduction to Academic Research
BMEG 490.description: Research project directed by a faculty member in Biomedical Engineering. Course may include workshops. Restricted to students with fourth-year standing or higher.

prerequisite.raw: Competitive GPA and permission from instructor

BMEG 490.prerequisiteText: Competitive GPA and permission from instructor

BMEG 495.title: Biomaterials
BMEG 495.description: Engineered materials in medical applications with an emphasis on material properties, functionality, design, and material response in the biological environment. .

BMEG 500.title: Orientation to Clinical Environment
BMEG 500.description: Operation of biomedical and clinical engineering facilities at hospitals. Daily activities of healthcare workers. Patients experience.

BMEG 501.title: Interdisciplinary Team Project in Medical Technology Innovation

BMEG 510.title: Anatomy and Physiology with Applications to Biomedical Devices
BMEG 510.description: Anatomical structures and physiological principles of major body systems. Functional connections to operation of diagnostic and therapeutic equipment. Exploration of recent advances.

BMEG 511.title: Fundamentals of Applied Pathophysiology in Biomedical Engineering

BMEG 521.title: Linear Systems in Optics
BMEG 521.description: Linear system theory and Fourier Optics, applications in optics including wave propagation and image quality assessment. ELEC_V 221 recommended.

BMEG 522.title: Modern Biomedical Optical Imaging
BMEG 522.description: Advanced multimodal optical imaging concepts, fundamental optics, optical OCT theories, advanced modern OCT technologies, and OCT application in clinical medicine and biomedical engineering. BMEG 421 or courses with MATLAB recommended.

BMEG 523.title: Clinical Informatics
BMEG 523.description: Fundamental concepts in clinical information systems, decision support, and mobile health. Application of information engineering to health care, including the management and use of patient health and well-being information.

BMEG 524.title: Genome Informatics
BMEG 524.description: Principles and best practices in analyzing genomics data. Genome architecture, mappability, repeat elements, ChIP-seq, open chromatin, histone modifications, single cell technologies, genome wide association studies, statistical analyses, computational analysis, data processing. BMEG 310 or equivalent recommended.

BMEG 556.title: Clinical and Industrial Biomedical Engineering
BMEG 556.description: Principles of professional engineering practice, the Canadian healthcare system, medical approach to diagnosis, principles and management of common medical devices, ethics and regulations for clinical trials, codes and regulations of medical devices, applications of biomedical engineering.

BMEG 557.title: Statistical Methods for Evaluating Medical Technologies

BMEG 580.title: Biomedical Engineering Topics at the Interface of Medicine and Engineering

BMEG 590.title: Biomedical Engineering Professional Skills
BMEG 590.description: Formulate and implement a professional skills development plan involving workshops on topics such as writing, presentation, teaching, finance, marketing, equity, ethics. Pass/Fail grading.

BMEG 597.title: Master of Engineering Project
BMEG 597.description: Supervised industrial, clinical, or research project for students registered in Biomedical Engineering program.

BMEG 598.title: Biomedical Engineering Seminar
BMEG 598.description: Presentation and discussion of current topics in biomedical engineering research and development. A required course for all graduate students in Biomedical Engineering.
